newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Clinton aide wants Ukraine to iron out corruption.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aide wants Ukraine to iron out corruption.

text.p: An aide to U.S. President Bill Clinton told Ukraine on Thursday to eliminate corruption if it wants to attract more investment.

"There are problems in various projects that are day-to-day, literally corruption and threats of violence," Richard Morningstar told a news conference after a four-day U.S.-Ukraine committee meeting on economic matters.
Ukraine has attracted only $1.5 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991.
Morningstar said he planned to raise the issue of corruption at a later meeting with President Leonid Kuchma.
Foreign and local investors say that bribes and dealing with mafia-like criminal gangs have come to be considered a normal part of doing business in Ukraine.

Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk told the news conference he did not deny the presence of corruption but criminal activity was a matter for the courts, not the government. "It has to be eliminated," he said.
Pynzenyk promised to reduce the number of licenses required to operate a business, eliminate permits to invest in Ukraine, deregulate some banking procedures, and simplify customs rules.
Morningstar also said Ukraine had large problems with bureaucracy and numerous regulations that hinder business.

"Ukraine can't expect large-scale investment while some of these problems exist," he said. "If some of these problems can be solved, that's a real opportunity to show the world that Ukraine is a place for investment."
